clue.text: Boss with itch reveals rash

parts.note: the head is the person in charge
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A manager scratching at a skin complaint that turns out to be a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Itch' reads as a noun beside 'rash', but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong decision is one taken hastily without thought, so rash is a synonym.

clue.text: Sitcom's Nora Batty ultimately wanting hormone replacement

indicators.note: the final letters are lacking, so the end of each name is dropped
a replacement puts things in different places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name without its last letter
the surname without its last letter

explanation.surface: A sitcom plot in which Nora Batty, the wrinkled-stockinged neighbour from Last of the Summer Wine, finally needs HRT.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is a character in the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, which is not the answer; 'ultimately' removes the last letter of both her names.
explanation.definitionFit: To the Manor Born is a classic BBC sitcom starring Penelope Keith, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Takes ecstasy — topless, when visiting Cyprus on vacation

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter is lost
a visitor goes inside, so this piece sits within the other
a place on vacation has been emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the island's name
rapture means ecstasy; topless loses its R

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Cyprus goes topless and takes drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecstasy' suggests the drug and the letter E, but it means raptures here.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture something is to take it, as a piece in chess or a prisoner in war.

clue.text: Offensive street artist content to leave Fringe

definitions.note: a noun here: a military attack

indicators.note: the inside of the word departs, so only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the word with its middle letters taken out

explanation.surface: A rude street artist happy to quit the Edinburgh Fringe festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy or willing, but it means the inside of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A strafe is an attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft, a kind of military offensive.

clue.text: 13 coaches moving Hearts up to be in a winning position

parts.note: 13 across is a bag, and a holdall is a type of bag

indicators.note: the hearts card symbol is shifted toward the front of the word, rearranging its order

parts.note: to coach is to teach; H stands for hearts in cards

explanation.surface: Bus companies relocating Heart of Midlothian, the Edinburgh football club, to a stronger league spot.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' points to the answer of 13 across, a word for which HOLDALL is a type. In TEACHES the H moves three places forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding all the aces is a card-game idiom for having every advantage and being sure to win.

clue.text: Star swimmer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a five-pointed star in heraldry
second meaning: a type of fish

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an Olympic champion in the pool; the heraldic sense of the first meaning is the hard part.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullet is both a heraldic star shape on a coat of arms and a common edible fish.

clue.text: Church backing poem about belief

indicators.note: going backwards, so the church letters are read from the end
turned about, so the poem is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A church supporting a poem about religious belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith, from the Latin for 'I believe', so a synonym of belief.

clue.text: Opportunists writing motor sport book inspired by graffiti artists

indicators.note: breathed in by, so this letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: taggers spray their signature tags on walls

explanation.surface: Chancers writing a motor-racing book inspired by street graffiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motor sport' looks like one phrase, but it splits into two pieces: motor and sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpetbaggers were Northerners who went South after the US Civil War for gain; the word now means any self-serving opportunist.

clue.text: Advanced laundry detergent assuming red playing surface?

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the detergent takes this piece inside it

parts.note: Surf is a British brand of washing powder
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-winger or red

explanation.surface: A new washing powder that copes with red stains on a sports pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Surf is a washing-powder brand sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Astroturf is a brand of artificial grass used for sports pitches; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Ben Folds Five working with a family member

indicators.note: letters set to work are moved about into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 5 down, the first word of that phrase

explanation.surface: The band Ben Folds Five collaborating with a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Folds Five is an American band; 'Five' is not part of the name here but a cross-reference to 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: One's own flesh and blood is an idiom for a close relative.

clue.text: Ended the burial at sea with boring patriotic display?

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so this letter goes inside the rest
being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dull naval funeral, the body committed to the sea with a flag-waving ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the burial so well it hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The colours of the Union Jack (and US flag) stand for patriotic bunting, so the phrase suggests a patriotic show.

clue.text: Start of economy drive with millions invested in online trade

indicators.note: the start is the opening letter, so only that one is taken
money invested is put inside, so these letters go into the word for drive

parts.note: to drive someone to act is to coerce them
M for million, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: An economy drive kick-started with millions put into internet commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Economy drive' reads as one phrase but splits between two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: E-commerce is buying and selling goods over the internet, which is online trade.

clue.text: Letter from occasionally sadistic husband

indicators.note: now and then means only every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: A note received from a cruel spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, but it means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelled-out name of the letter H, so it names one letter.

clue.text: See 5
Airline good to land

explanation.surface: An airline managing to touch down safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' suggests a plane arriving, but it means to catch or secure, as with a fish or a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something and to land it both mean to secure or capture it.

clue.text: Perhaps airline's opening new line after awful riots

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An airline launching a new route after terrible riots.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'airline' as air line, the passage carrying air into the body; 'Perhaps' marks the answer as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nostril is an external opening of the respiratory passage, so it opens an airway.

clue.text: Bad drivers rowed loudly — silence shrouding journey the other way

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: said the same as a word for a highway

indicators.note: going in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards
a shroud wraps around, so one piece encloses the next

parts.note: a go is a turn or trip

explanation.surface: Bad drivers argued noisily, then fell silent on a journey back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowed' tempts the sense of quarrelling (rhymes with cowed), but the sound wanted is the boat-rowing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a selfish, reckless driver who takes up more than their share of the road.

clue.text: Tory do

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a Conservative party event; 'do' is a verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Con is the abbreviation for a Conservative, and to con someone is to do them out of something.

clue.text: Palace a pushover? Withdraw article to show respect

indicators.note: pulling out a word like 'a' or 'the' removes it from what precedes

parts.note: easy, with its article A taken out

explanation.surface: Crystal Palace, the London football club, are easy opponents, so a pundit should retract his piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The article removed is the letter A. Crystal Palace is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy is polite consideration, so showing it is showing respect.

clue.text: Someone likely to have some Sega merchandise

definitions.text: Someone likely to have some Sega merchandise

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken, a run of their letters

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Profiling a likely owner of Sega products.
explanation.walkthrough: Sega is a Japanese video-game company, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A video-game player is exactly the person who would own consoles and games made by Sega.

clue.text: I like a bloke boxing, generally

indicators.note: to box is to put in a case, so this word encloses the letter

parts.note: in the way of a man

explanation.surface: Someone admitting a general fondness for a bloke who boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I like' looks like the start of a sentence; I is the letter, and 'like a bloke' is one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly means for the most part, which is what generally means.

clue.text: One appears with a shot drink on the counter containing small amount of garlic?

indicators.note: counter suggests going against the direction of reading, so the letters run backwards
holding inside, so the next letter goes into the reversed drink

parts.note: a half is a half-pint of beer
garlic is bought as a bulb of cloves

explanation.surface: A shot drink served at the bar, laced with a little garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a drink, but in the definition it means a photograph; 'small amount' splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashbulb is the old disposable bulb that fires a burst of light as a photo is taken.

clue.text: Ban because of British papers

parts.note: 'for' can mean because of, as in 'jailed for theft'

explanation.surface: A prohibition imposed due to British newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid something is to prohibit it, which is what ban means as a verb.

clue.text: Dicky Attenborough regularly tried to make military show

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are put out of order
at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: Richard Attenborough, nicknamed Dickie, made efforts to stage a military pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like Lord Attenborough's nickname, but it is British slang for faulty and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is an annual display of military bands staged at Edinburgh Castle.

clue.text: See 2
Wild spending increasing across Premier League primarily

indicators.note: stretching over something, so this word straddles the initials
in the first place, so only the initial letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the initials of the two words

explanation.surface: Reckless transfer spending growing throughout English top-flight football.
explanation.definitionFit: Splurging is spending money freely and extravagantly, which is wild spending.

clue.text: Return envelope ready for posting and journalist is relaxed

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read from the end

explanation.surface: A writer relieved to send back a stamped addressed envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: An SAE is the stamped addressed envelope you enclose for a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, a synonym of relaxed.
